messages:
mike: Heads up — we need project approvals + GCP quota increases to consolidate EU inference capacity into a shared pool. Projects involved: proj-redwood-eu-01 (123456789012) and proj-redwood-eu-burst (123456789013).

mike: Requested resources (initial ask): A100 x24, H100 x8, L4 x80, TPU v4 x4. Also need 6 static NAT IPs for egress and an egress quota bump to ~50TB/month. Purpose: Dedicated cluster migration + canary/burst fleet for new EU customers. Rough delta in infra spend ~ $65k/mo. Need infra + security + finance OK before I file with GCP.

infra-bot: Draft quota request created: Q-2026-5823. Auto-check: billing account not linked for proj-redwood-eu-burst (123456789013). Please attach billing account or request will be rejected. Estimated GCP review time: 48-72h.

sara: quick q: why both H100 and A100? can some of the burst be L4 instead (cheaper) for short jobs?

mike: H100s are for latency-sensitive RLHF workloads where throughput/mem matters; A100s are for long training-ish inference (large context), L4s for lower-cost embeddings/embedding rerank. We want mix to optimize cost/latency.

morgan: I'd rather not create a new proj-redwood-eu-burst if we can reuse gpu-burst-eu (proj 123450000111) — avoids another billing attachment step. Any constraints on per-project quota that require new project?

mike: main reason for new project was isolation for customers during rollouts. But if reuse is faster for quota approval, fine. tradeoff: isolation vs speed.

jia: Need the steady vs burst breakdown (p95 vs average). Also add fallback model variants and autoscale policy so security knows we won't accidentally OOM. Can you paste the capacity plan?

mike: TL;DR capacity plan: steady = A100 x8 + L4 x20; burst capacity = A100 + H100 + L4 to reach totals above. Peak concurrent nodes expected 40 GPUs, sustained 12-16.

mike: I'll attach a short JSON payload we'll submit to GCP (for reviewer):
```
{
  "projects": [
    {"id": "123456789012", "region": "europe-west3", "quotas": [{"metric": "A100_GPUS", "limit": 24}, {"metric": "L4_GPUS", "limit": 50}]},
    {"id": "123456789013", "region": "europe-west3", "quotas": [{"metric": "H100_GPUS", "limit": 8}, {"metric": "TPU_V4", "limit": 4}, {"metric": "NAT_IPS", "limit": 6}]}
  ]
}
```
(We won't actually paste this into the GCP form verbatim, it's the internal ask structure.)

kevin: Are preemptible or spot GPUs acceptable for the burst portion? If yes we should mark those explicitly to reduce committed spend.

mike: Yes, most burst L4+some A100 can be preemptible. H100 and a subset of A100 need to be on-demand for SLAs. I'll annotate in the submission.

sara: Security ask: for the 6 static NAT IPs — do we plan shared VPC or private egress? we need SAML + VPC-SC considerations documented for the private deployment.

morgan: If we reuse gpu-burst-eu we already have shared VPC scoping and 2 reserved egress IPs. We still need 4 more. That saves time.

jia: Finance: please confirm cost center 7012 covers the extra $65k/mo delta; cc @finance. Also include the projected 3-month burn and rollback plan if costs spike.

mike: I'll ping finance and attach the burn projection. ETA to submit to GCP if we get all approvals: today EOD. Will include justification, autoscaling policy, preemptible flags, and security runbook link.

infra-bot: Reminder: for NAT IPs we need the exact names and regions; GCP requires one reserve per region. Also flag for egress quota requests: provide sample day-by-day traffic profile (CSV) or they'll ask for it.

mike: Noted. I'll attach daily-traffic.csv and the runbook. Submitting draft now. I'll paste ticket link once created. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: GCP case created: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/987654321 — Case Q-2026-5823 submitted. Current status: UNDER_REVIEW. Expected response window 72 hours.

sara: acked. please put the ticket number in the infra-runbook and notify oncall if review requires a networking change. :white_check_mark:

mike: thanks all — filing now and will update thread with the GCP case link and any follow-ups.
